Reinforced by repeated use of “strong,” this FOMC statement conveys a clearly positive macro backdrop: robust labor markets, solid spending and investment, and inflation near the symmetric 2% goal. In the academic lens, such language and the decision to hike are consistent with Taylor-rule style normalization when output is strong and inflation is on target (Taylor; Clarida, Galí, and Gertler). The operational details—raising IOER to 2.20% and using ON RRP—reflect the floor-system mechanics discussed by Goodfriend (2002), while the phrase “further gradual increases” works through the expectations channel and the term structure (Cochrane and Piazzesi), helping to anchor inflation expectations around target (inflation-targeting literature; Walsh/Cecchetti). The primary credit rate remaining above the funds rate is in line with a penalty-rate framework rooted in Bagehot’s principle. Overall, the communication is optimistic with balanced risks—bullish, not exuberant.

“Household spending and business fixed investment have grown strongly.”
